subject.title: fix(codex): bound app-server websocket handshake waits at 30s

question: Should Codex app-server WebSocket opening handshakes use an unconditional 30-second ws-layer deadline with exit as the authoritative terminal signal?
rationale: The patch correctly bounds an indefinite wait, but the exact fixed deadline and error-versus-exit semantics affect existing remote WebSocket setups and must compose with the higher-level initialize/startup deadlines owned by the Codex client.

options.title: Accept the 30-second transport deadline
options.body: After splitting the APNs change, keep the shared 30-second ws handshake timeout and current exit semantics for both TCP and Unix transports.

options.title: Derive from the existing startup budget
options.body: Replace the independent fixed deadline with a value derived from an existing Codex initialization or startup deadline so timeout ownership remains centralized.

options.title: Pause for live backend validation
options.body: Require a live Codex app-server TCP and Unix-socket run before selecting the permanent timeout and terminal-event contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second transport deadline
recommendation.body: After splitting the APNs change, keep the shared 30-second ws handshake timeout and current exit semantics for both TCP and Unix transports.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history shows direct merger and revision ownership of the Codex app-server transport and client integration.
